The EAGLE team’s goal is to eliminate leaded aviation fuels in piston-engine aircraft safely by the end of 2030. To achieve the lead-free goal, EAGLE will: ​ Identify at least one unleaded fuel acceptable for safe General Aviation fleet use. Facilitate the increased production, distribution and greater use of unleaded replacement fuels. Ensure that 100 low-lead fuel is available during the transition to unleaded fuel. Establish policies that support airport infrastructure funding for unleaded fuel. Endorse plans that reduce or eliminate reliance upon leaded aviation fuels. Satellite imagery, GIS, GPS, and drones all provide the ability to gather information about the scene. However, when a disaster happens indoors, none of those capabilities carry over. The available data becomes 2D, typically a blueprint if it exists, and does not include standpipes, shutoffs, alarm panels, or AEDs. These missing elements are necessary for a safe and timely response by first responders. Without indoor spatial intelligence, responders must make high stakes and high-risk decisions with incomplete information. pages.text: Building Public Data for LLMs – Open Source Initiative Building Public Data for LLMs Part of the Deep Dive: Data Governance Webinar Series As the capabilities and influence of large language models (LLMs) continue to expand, so too do the risks associated with opaque, legally ambiguous, and unrepresentative training data. While much attention has been focused on open-source models, relatively little infrastructure exists to support high-quality open datasets for pretraining. Drawing on EleutherAI’s work on the Common Pile, an 8 TB, openly licensed dataset designed for LLM training, I will outline a principled approach to constructing, curating, and evaluating open datasets that are legal, transparent, and representative. The Common Pile serves as a case study for how community-driven, auditable pipelines can be used to aggregate and filter data from public domain and openly licensed sources. Such wheels therefore will only run on the system on which they are built. See the pypackaging-native content under “Building and installing or uploading artifacts” for more context on that. A wheel like that is therefore an intermediate stage to producing a binary that can be distributed. That final binary may be a wheel - in that case, run auditwheel (Linux), delocate (macOS) or delvewheel (Windows) to vendor the required shared libraries into the wheel. The final binary may also be in another packaging format (e.g., a .rpm , .deb or .conda package). In that case, there are packaging ecosystem-specific tools to first install the wheel into a staging area, then making the extension modules in that install location relocatable (e.g., by rewriting RPATHs), and then repackaging it into the final package format.

The tool can be accessed at https://bds.explorer.ces.census.gov . All tabulations in BDS Explorer are sourced from the Census API's BDS endpoint . BDS Explorer provides access to the entire BDS dataset via line charts, bar charts, and thematic maps. The application's intuitive dashboard allows for the construction of tables and charts to compare and rank measures of business dynamism such as employment, job creation and destruction, and firm births and deaths across a wide range of establishment and firm characteristics. Potential analyses include a longitudinal look at job creation by establishment age across counties, ranking establishment entry rates of young firms across NAICS industry groups and comparing job destruction rates by firm sizes across a selection of Metropolitan Areas. The BDS-SU-REV provides year-over-year changes in employment, payroll, and revenue for each quarter of the year for businesses that operate in one location (single-units) and file their taxes under a single Employer Identification Number (EIN). This product relies on IRS annual tax filings to collect revenue information and IRS quarterly tax filings to collect employment and payroll information for the pay periods including March 12 th , June 12 th , September 12 th , and December 12 th . Year-over-year employment and payroll changes are calculated between the same point in year t and year t-1 (i.e., June 12 th year t-1 to June 12 th year t, etc.). Employment and payroll growth is labeled as job and pay creation respectively and employment and payroll decline as job and pay destruction. A novel innovation in the BDS-SU-REV is the incorporation of annual revenue data for single-establishment firms that consistently maintain positive employment levels each quarter. A positive annual growth in revenue is categorized as revenue creation, while negative growth is categorized as revenue destruction. Jump to: Data Definitions

pages.text: Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) Data Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) Data Skip Navigation Business Trends and Outlook Survey (BTOS) Data July 13, 2026 The Business Trends and Outlook Survey provides high-frequency, nationally representative data on U.S. employer businesses. The survey provides local, state, and federal officials near real-time data for policy and decision-making including after natural disasters or during economic crises. The BTOS also provides insights into business recovery after these events. The BTOS sample consists of approximately 1.2 million businesses split into six panels (approximately 200,000 cases per panel). Businesses in each panel are asked to report once every 12 weeks over the course of one year. Data collection occurs every two weeks. The BTOS is comprised of a set of core questions and supplemental content, which is added as needed. The BTOS collects information on a broad range of business conditions. Topics include current performance, changes in revenue, employment, hours worked, demand, and prices. For most concepts, businesses are asked about the previous two weeks and for a 6-month outlook. Data collected from September 11, 2023 to present include all employer businesses (single location and multi-location) in the U.S. economy, excluding farms. pages.text: But I'm a Cheerleader | Movies | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Movies This article is more than 25 years old Review But I'm a Cheerleader This article is more than 25 years old Peter Bradshaw Thu 12 Apr 2001 21.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google D irector and co-writer Jamie Babbit makes her feature debut with this satire of America's creepy Christian "sexual reorientation" camps, where confused teens are sent so that their nascent gayness can be deprogrammed out of them. Natasha Lyonne plays Megan, a cheerleader who hugs her fellow pom-pom-botherers inappropriately and hates making out with her jock boyfriend. He and Megan's family arrange an "intervention" where she is confronted with her shameful tendencies and sent to the True Directions camp, run by two smug tyrants in Straight Is Great T-shirts, played by Cathy Moriarty and RuPaul (here out of drag), clearly repressed gays themselves. Once there, Megan falls for a girl with the interesting name of Graham, played by Clea DuVall. As in all therapy boot-camp movies - such as Girl, Interrupted, in which DuVall had a role - there has to be a wild child with whom the heroine makes a connection. This is Graham's role. It's reasonably amusing, with 2-D acting and writing, and Day-Glo pink and blue colour schemes. But it could have been funnier, and I would have preferred to know more in documentary terms about the actual reality of these terrible camps, rather than sit through this heavy-handed and oddly lenient comedy. pages.text: Buying a Train Ticket | National Rail Skip to main content Buying a Ticket Find the best train ticket for you Want to know what ticket types are available, how much they cost, and where and when you can buy and use them? Then read on. Which train ticket is the best choice for me? As a general rule, the earlier you can buy a ticket, the better the price you can get. If you know the date and time you wish to travel, then an Advance ticket will be suitable. For more flexibility, Off-Peak and Super Off-Peak tickets and Anytime tickets will be a better option, as you are not limited to a specific date or train. For more information about getting the most affordable ticket for your journey, see below. Advance tickets These must be bought in advance and are only valid on the date and train specified. They are sold in limited numbers, subject to availability and on a first come, first served basis. You can usually buy an Advance ticket up to 12 weeks ahead of travel, and they are still available until the day of travel on many routes – sometimes up to 10 minutes before departure. They offer a great deal if you know exactly when you want to travel. Find out more about Advance tickets . Off-Peak and Super Off-Peak tickets These good value tickets can be bought at any time and allow you to travel on any permitted train during off-peak hours. If an Off-Peak or Super Off-Peak ticket is available for your journey, journey planners will make them available to purchase. In general, Off-Peak hours begin at 09:30 from Monday to Friday in cities and large towns, and at 09:00 everywhere else.

pages.title: By Land and Sea—17 European Trips From London | National Geographic
pages.description: Whether it’s a short hop across the Channel or an overland expedition to the furthest reaches of Europe, some of the richest travel experiences happen when you skip the flight.
pages.text: By Land and Sea—17 European Trips From London | National Geographic By Oliver Smith Published October 24, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Today, it’s easier to travel further and faster around Europe than ever before — to board a flight and effectively parachute yourself into a new destination. But by travelling overland, be it by ferry, train or car, on a bike or on foot, you’re able to observe the slow, subtle changes at ground level with every accumulated mile. Overland travel by rail is also easier than it’s ever been, thanks to an ever-expanding network of high-speed and sleeper trains across Europe. You might board a morning Eurostar at London St Pancras International and that same day be joining a midnight crawl of Madrid’s tapas bars or standing beneath Milan’s hulking Duomo as stars twinkle above its white marble facade. Ferries, too, offer perspectives unfamiliar to those at the cruising altitude of an airliner, whether that’s witnessing the green coast of northern Spain unravelling out of the blue horizons of Biscay or seeing Icelandic volcanoes peek over grey North Atlantic waves. United States Department of Transportation In This Section Cabin Air Quality Thursday, September 4, 2025 The FAA is committed to protecting the safety and health of passengers and cabin crews on our nation's airlines. The agency has strict cabin air standards , and studies have shown cabin air is as good as or better than the air found in offices and homes. In rare instances, mechanical issues such as failures of an engine oil seal or recirculation fan bearings can cause fumes to enter the cabin. Airlines are required to report these incidents to the FAA. The FAA investigates the causes and makes sure they’re fixed before the aircraft returns to service. Background The FAA requires airplane manufacturers to show that the crew and passenger compartment air is free from harmful or hazardous concentrations of smoke, vapor, or toxic or noxious fumes during normal operating conditions and in the event of any probable failure conditions. FAA regulations require airliners' ventilation systems to supply clean air to both passengers and crew members. United States Department of Transportation In This Section Caitlin Locke Associate Administrator, Aviation Safety Caitlin Locke serves as Associate Administrator for the FAA’s Aviation Safety Organization (AVS-1), a position she has held since June 2026. Locke leads the office responsible for the certification, production approval, and continued airworthiness of aircraft; and certification of pilots, mechanics, and others in safety-related positions. Previously, Locke was Executive Director for Aircraft Certification Service (AIR), overseeing type certification, production approval, airworthiness certification, and continued airworthiness of the U.S. civil aircraft fleet, including both commercial and general aviation . Before that, Locke served as Director of AIR’s Compliance & Airworthiness Division, where she managed a broad portfolio of certification and validation projects. Earlier in her FAA career, Locke served as acting deputy executive director and chief of staff of Flight Standards. She also served as Deputy Executive Director of the Office of Rulemaking, and as a Senior Technical Advisor in AVS. Locke joined the FAA in 2008. The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) has completed the sale of approximately 2.97 acres of federal land at the Calcasieu Pass Radio Beacon Station in Cameron Parish, Louisiana. The sale returns an isolated federal parcel to productive use and supports development of adjacent energy infrastructure. The parcel was originally reserved in 1875 for lighthouse operations and later managed by the U.S. Coast Guard. On July 3, 2025, the Coast Guard formally notified the BLM that it no longer had an operational need for the property and intended to relinquish custody, accountability, and control of the land.
